detail.longDescription: I wanted to know who introduced this function . Therefore, I used git blame to work out the commit that introduced that function , i.e. b87bdb9ebd44b4494e3e9e9c304d4dbf8810905f . However, that commit was merged in via this PR , created by somebody and merged by a maintainer . The point is that the such a PR is formed by 76 commits not all authored by the PR's creator, and none of which is b87bdb9ebd44b4494e3e9e9c304d4dbf8810905f . Of those commits I wanted to know which one specifically introduced that line. Eventually I found it by scrolling through the list of commits from that PR , it is af34f069e9d410001b313518502534ab8a9351b1 . I'd argue, however, that a more natural workflow is to single out the file in the "Files changed" tab and then to click somewhere to say "show me the commits that contributed to this file change". How can I do that? Or what other workflow is advisable in such a scenario?
